static_traits.name: Zhou Li
static_traits.family_status: High family support, but has not yet discussed inner fears with family
static_traits.medical_history: Broke an arm skiing, fully recovered; No major physical illness; no psychotherapy received in the past
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to describe experiences and thoughts concretely; slightly tense at first visit, but highly cooperative, willing to explore and reflect

basic_info.main_problem: I have been struggling with self-doubt and the fear that 'I may never win a ski race', even though I often place second.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because these negative thoughts are affecting my performance and enjoyment in skiing competitions.
growth_experiences: A skiing accident fractured my arm. Though fully recovered physically, the event became an important psychological turning point, after which persistent fear and self-doubt arose in race-related situations; a recent near-victory still ending in second place further reinforced worries of 'never winning'.

core_beliefs: I lack the talent to win races
I am not good enough / not competent enough

special_situations.event: Finished second in the most recent evenly matched competition
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am not first, it means I am not good enough and lack talent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Tries to improve performance to win the championship through stricter self-demands and visualization training
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: You failed again; second place means nothing

special_situations.event: The preparation phase before each competition
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If fear and doubt appear before a race, it means I am not suited for this sport and will never win
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly thinks it over before competitions and talks with peers to seek confirmation, but still insists on 'whether to win the championship' as the only criterion
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I'll never win; I have no talent

special_situations.event: Thinking about my future in skiing
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot become champion in the future, then present efforts are meaningless
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focusing goals solely on 'must win the championship', ignoring achievements and progress along the way
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I can't win, effort is meaningless

special_situations.event: Family and teammates' positive feedback and affirmation about recent competitions
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I haven't won championships, others' praise doesn't count and doesn't prove I am good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Questioning others' evaluations, using only ranking as the measurement standard
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They're just comforting me; second place doesn't deserve praise

core_conflict.wish: Desiring to be recognized as a 'winner', proving I have ability and talent
core_conflict.fear: Fearing failure and being seen as not good enough, worrying about never winning a race
defense_goal: Trying to control uncertainty and lower anxiety by maintaining strict binary standards (not winning equals failure) and harsh self-criticism

object_relations.self_representation: Not-good-enough competitor, someone who could fail at any time
object_relations.object_representation: Well-meaning others (family/teammates) who cannot truly understand my inner struggle

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor encourages him to focus on the positive and reframe his view of second place
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing that 'not winning means not deserving affirmation', seeing second place as failure (transference: seeing external affirmation as unreal)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using an inquiring, gently supportive tone, first empathizing with their subjective experience of 'failure', then gradually guiding differentiation of facts from interpretations, returning to concrete evidence and progress markers.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked whether they are willing to discuss competition fears with supportive family members
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Worrying that family won't understand or will minimize her feelings, hence choosing not to express them
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Inviting identification of repressed emotions and needs in a safe, nonjudgmental way, using gentle open-ended questions, allowing silence, encouraging gradual expression through 'I feel...' statements.

manifestations: Repeated thoughts of 'if I can't win, effort is meaningless' after placing second
Treats winning and losing as the only value, ignoring process and growth
outcomes: Heightened anxiety before and after races
Reduced sense of enjoyment and impaired motivation in competitions

manifestations: Having a supportive family but not discussing inner fears and self-doubt with them
Even with positive team feedback, still finding it hard to accept recognition; inner experience disconnected from external evaluation
outcomes: Subjective support below objective support levels

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Takes 'only winning the championship counts as good' as an absolute standard
Internalizes 'second place = failure' as a self-judgment rule, ignoring other positive evidence (such as improved personal records)

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Not expressing fears and worries to family, turning pressure and self-blame against the self
Being more self-critical rather than seeking external support when anxious

positive_force: Has won second place multiple times in high-level competition, with stable competitive ability
Able to identify improved personal records and progress after races
Actively seeking counseling, trying visualization and communicating with peers
negative_force: Black-and-white perfectionist standards (not winning equals failure)
Overgeneralization and mental filtering, ignoring positive evidence
Ongoing worry about 'never winning' and emotional reasoning
Sleep disorder and anxiety impairing state and performance

target_behavior.behavior: Intense self-denying automatic thoughts and anxiety before and after races
antecedent: After competitions, especially when getting second place
Thinking about my future ski career
target_behavior.core_reason: After the history of a skiing injury became a psychological turning point, the rigid evaluative standard 'I must win the championship' formed, accompanied by overgeneralization, mental filtering, and black-and-white thinking, leading to catastrophic interpretations of one's own ability
target_behavior.function: Escaping and suppressing uncertainty and failure, trying to maintain control and drive through harsh self-criticism
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased enjoyment of racing, affected performance, intensified and persistent anxiety, reinforced negative self-concept

target_behavior.behavior: Sleep disorder (difficulty falling asleep due to worries of 'never winning' and self-denying thoughts)
antecedent: Repeatedly dwelling on 'never winning' scenarios at night
Excessive rumination on rankings after competitions
target_behavior.core_reason: Excessive worry about failure and cognitive biases (mental filtering, overgeneralization, black-and-white thinking) cause high arousal and persistent rumination
target_behavior.function: Subjectively trying to gain a sense of control through thinking and rehearsal, but actually worsening anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Declining sleep quality, daytime fatigue and increased anxiety, further affecting training and race performance
